items.followUp: What is the role of bile in digestion?

rubric.why: HCl provides the acidic conditions needed for pepsin to work and activates pepsinogen.
rubric.description: States that HCl provides an acidic medium or activates pepsinogen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the role of HCl in creating an acidic medium or activating pepsinogen; accept either idea clearly stated.

rubric.why: Pepsin is the protein-digesting enzyme in the stomach.
rubric.description: States that pepsin digests proteins into simpler products.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying proteins as the substrate and peptides or peptones as the products.

modelAnswer: HCl provides an acidic medium in the stomach and activates pepsinogen into pepsin.
Pepsin digests proteins into simpler substances such as peptides or peptones.

items.followUp: What is goitre, and what can cause it?

rubric.why: Iodine is needed by the thyroid gland to make thyroxine.
rubric.description: Connects iodine deficiency with reduced thyroxine production.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that iodine is required to produce thyroxine or thyroid hormone.

rubric.why: The characteristic effect of iodine deficiency is enlargement of the thyroid gland.
rubric.description: Identifies thyroid enlargement (goitre) as an effect of iodine deficiency.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming goitre or describing enlargement/swelling of the thyroid gland.

modelAnswer: Iodine is required by the thyroid gland to produce thyroxine; its deficiency reduces thyroxine production.
The thyroid gland may enlarge, causing goitre.

items.followUp: How can excessive transpiration affect a plant?

rubric.why: Transpiration can remove water faster than the roots replace it.
rubric.description: Explains that transpiration may cause excessive water loss.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying excessive water loss or water loss that exceeds absorption.

rubric.why: Severe water loss causes wilting and can damage or kill the plant.
rubric.description: States a harmful consequence of excessive water loss.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for wilting, dehydration, or possible death of the plant.

modelAnswer: If transpiration is excessive, water may be lost faster than it is absorbed by the roots.
This causes the plant to wilt and, in severe cases, may lead to its death.

items.followUp: How can red blood cells and white blood cells be separated from blood?

rubric.why: Centrifugation is the method used to separate blood components by density.
rubric.description: Names centrifugation as the separation method.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming centrifugation or use of a centrifuge.

rubric.why: Centrifugation separates the denser cells from the less dense plasma.
rubric.description: Describes where the blood cells and plasma are found after centrifugation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that cells settle at the bottom and plasma remains as the upper layer/supernatant.

modelAnswer: Blood is placed in a tube and centrifuged.
The denser blood cells settle at the bottom, while plasma remains as the upper layer (supernatant).

items.followUp: How does pericardial fluid protect the heart?

rubric.why: The fluid allows the heart to move smoothly as it beats.
rubric.description: States that pericardial fluid lubricates the heart or reduces friction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the fluid with lubrication or reduced friction during heartbeats.

rubric.why: The fluid cushions the heart and helps protect it during movement.
rubric.description: States a protective or cushioning function of the fluid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it cushions/protects the heart or helps it beat smoothly.

modelAnswer: Pericardial fluid lubricates the heart and reduces friction as it beats.
It also cushions and protects the heart.

items.followUp: Name five professions related to biology and briefly state what two of them involve.

rubric.why: Biology provides entry into a range of professional fields.
rubric.description: Names two valid biology-related professions.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for any two distinct valid professions; examples include medicine, agriculture, fisheries, forestry, animal husbandry and biotechnology.

rubric.why: A brief description shows how biological knowledge is applied in professional work.
rubric.description: Gives relevant applications or roles for two professions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for each relevant description of a profession, up to 2 marks; examples include diagnosing/treating patients, improving crops, managing fish or forests, caring for livestock, or applying biology in biotechnology.

rubric.why: A fifth valid profession completes the requested range of career options.
rubric.description: Names one additional distinct biology-related profession.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one further valid profession not already counted.

modelAnswer: Biological studies can lead to professions such as medicine and surgery, agriculture, fisheries, forestry, animal husbandry and biotechnology.
Medical professionals use biological knowledge to diagnose and treat patients.
Agricultural professionals apply biology to improve crops and farming.
Other options include managing fisheries, forests and livestock, or working in biotechnology.

items.followUp: Compare the functions of chloroplasts and leucoplasts.

rubric.why: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis.
rubric.description: Explains the pigment and function of chloroplasts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking chlorophyll in chloroplasts with photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Chromoplast pigments give colour to plant parts.
rubric.description: Explains the pigment-related role of chromoplasts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that chromoplasts contain coloured pigments or impart colour.

rubric.why: Leucoplasts are colourless plastids commonly involved in food storage.
rubric.description: Explains a characteristic and/or function of leucoplasts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying leucoplasts as colourless or stating their food-storage role.

rubric.why: Examples of stored food clarify the function of leucoplasts.
rubric.description: Names a food substance stored by leucoplasts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming starch, oil or protein as a stored substance.

modelAnswer: Chloroplasts are green plastids containing chlorophyll; they carry out photosynthesis.
Chromoplasts contain coloured pigments and give colour to flowers, fruits and other plant parts.
Leucoplasts are colourless plastids that store food such as starch, oil or protein.

items.followUp: State five characteristics of enzymes and explain why temperature affects their activity.

rubric.why: Enzymes are biological catalysts and are generally proteins.
rubric.description: Identifies enzymes as catalysts and states their protein nature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the catalyst role and 1 mark for stating that enzymes are proteins.

rubric.why: Specificity, reusability and effectiveness in small amounts are key enzyme characteristics.
rubric.description: States two further valid characteristics of enzymes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for each of two valid characteristics, such as substrate specificity, remaining unchanged after a reaction, being reusable, or acting in small amounts.

rubric.why: Enzyme activity depends on temperature, and excessive heat can change enzyme shape.
rubric.description: States a valid effect of temperature on enzyme activity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that activity changes with temperature, identifying an optimum temperature, or stating that high temperature denatures enzymes.

modelAnswer: Enzymes are biological catalysts and are generally proteins.
Each enzyme is specific to its substrate or reaction.
Enzymes can act in small amounts and remain unchanged after a reaction, so they can be reused.
Their activity is affected by temperature and pH, and each enzyme works best under optimum conditions.
High temperatures can denature an enzyme and reduce or stop its activity.
